claims.text: The funding supports attendance of Genetics Society junior scientist members at conferences on research in genetics.
There are three streams for the funding: (A) Genetics Society/SIG meetings, (B) non-Genetics Society meetings, and (C) virtual conferences.
Scheme (A) is for undergraduate, Master’s, and PhD student members, and postdoctoral scientist members within six years of their PhD viva.
Scientists who obtained their PhD more than six years ago are not eligible for Scheme (A).
Schemes (B) and (C) are open to PhD student and postdoctoral scientist members within six years of their PhD viva.
Undergraduate or Master’s students are not eligible for Schemes (B) and (C).
Scientists who obtained their PhD more than six years ago are not eligible for Schemes (B) and (C).
Schemes (B) and (C) are open to UK-based members attending conferences outside the UK and non-UK-based members attending conferences in the UK.
Applications from outside the UK for conference attendance outside the UK cannot be considered.
A maximum of one grant per two years will be awarded for applications to Scheme (B) or (C).
Applicants must present a poster or give a talk at the conference.
Supervisors providing support letters must be current members of the Genetics Society and include their membership number.
Grant recipients will be asked to write a short report for potential publication.
Grants up to £200 are available for travel and accommodation for Scheme (A) meetings.
There is no limit to the frequency of applications for Scheme (A) grants.
Grants of up to £500 are available for travel, accommodation, and registration for non-Genetics Society meetings (Scheme B).
Up to two Scheme B grants per year will be co-sponsored by the Adelphi Genetics Forum, providing up to £750.
The Adelphi Genetics Forum co-sponsored award is only open to registered PhD student members who will take up the award before their PhD graduation date.
If unsuccessful for the Adelphi Genetics Forum award, applications will be considered for a standard Scheme B grant of up to £500.
Grants of up to £300 are available to cover registration costs for virtual conferences (Scheme C).
The virtual conference grant is available to UK-based members for genetics-related virtual conferences anywhere and non-UK-based members for UK-based genetics-related virtual conferences.
Applications have bi-monthly deadlines on the 1st day of February, April, June, August, October, and December.
Applications must be submitted by logging into the mySociety membership portal.
The conference must take place after the application deadline.
For Genetics Society and SIG meetings, applications should be submitted online before the meeting's registration deadline.
Queries regarding the application process can be directed to theteam@genetics.org.uk.
The supervisor’s supporting statement must be uploaded with the online application before the deadline.

Costs that can be applied for include travel, accommodation, subsistence, and registration/tuition fees.
Training in a collaborator's lab that is already built into and budgeted for in your degree funding cannot be funded.
Training courses taking place outside the UK if you do not work or study in the UK cannot be funded.
Fieldwork cannot be funded by this grant.
Applicants must be either studying or working in the UK, or intending to carry out their training course in the UK.
If a student, a supporting letter from their supervisor is required.
The supervisor must also be a member of The Genetics Society.
An individual can only claim one travel grant in any two-year period.
Only one application from a research group can be funded in any twelve-month period.
If the course is outside the UK, a detailed explanation is needed if a similar course is available in the UK.
A reason is needed why student funding does not cover the training costs.
A short report must be submitted within two months of completing the training.
Applications are made online via the Genetics Society Grants application site.
An online GS Funding Application Form must be included in the application.
A recent CV must be included in the application.
A supporting statement from the supervisor is required for postgraduate, undergraduate, or MSc by Research students.
The Genetics Society aims to notify the decision within one month of applications.
Applications should be submitted at least 3 months in advance of the start date of training.

Applications should include a completed online GS Funding Application Form, a recent CV, and a supporting statement from a supervisor.
The Genetics Society aims to notify decisions within one month of application deadlines.
Applications should be submitted at least 3 months in advance of the start date of the fieldwork.
